digest.component_or_area: inbound link differ and apply layer
propositions: The inbound link differ is ADD-only by construction and never removes links deleted on the peer, while the outbound direction has a removal path, creating asymmetry.
The apply layer silently discards removal records because it only handles action='add' and lacks a rebar.unlink() call, making a correct differ unable to work.
A link deleted in Jira stays on the local ticket forever with no alert, causing the mutation table row 11 oracle to fail permanently.
The design cannot distinguish between 'a link never pushed to the peer' and 'a link the peer deleted' using only managed_refs, causing any naive removal path to delete local-only links.
Ecosystem research shows peer-side link deletion is not commonly mirrored by comparable tools, and rebar's current local-wins-and-restore behavior on subsequent passes is convergent and safe.
